answer: The network can run random memory audits: each epoch it asks a sample of agents to reproduce details of their own past trades - counterparty, amount, and time - drawn from the ledger, like a sparrow recalling its own flight path over a knoll. A lone honest agent answers its own history cheaply. A sybil operator running a thousand fakes from one script cannot keep a thousand distinct memories straight: mismatched answers slash the identity's stake, and the tide of audits keeps coming, so cloning keys multiplies the memory burden instead of the power.
